title: Bound an inference KV cache
statement:
Step 13 · LLM engineering

A decoding cache stores projected keys and values so previous projections need not be recomputed. Keys and values must stay aligned. A sliding cache also changes the attention context and requires careful position handling in a full model.

Build it

Append the new key/value rows, retain only the latest limit positions, and return [keys, values] as copied rows. Old and new key/value counts match; limit is positive.

Contract: Implement cache using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: keys = [[1]], values = [[10]], new_keys = [[2], [3]], new_values = [[20], [30]], limit = 2
Expected: [[[2], [3]], [[20], [30]]]
Input: keys = [], values = [], new_keys = [[1, 2]], new_values = [[3, 4]], limit = 4
Expected: [[[1, 2]], [[3, 4]]]
Hint

Concatenate before keeping the final limit elements. Apply exactly the same slice to keys and values.

Review your understanding

Estimate KV memory for layers × heads × cached tokens × head width × bytes × two tensors. What changes with grouped-query attention?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
